Team,

Initial findings from the cluster: during the 02:00–07:00 UTC window we observed:
- a sudden shift in sequence-length distribution for MapSync requests (avg tokens +180%) causing larger-than-expected KV cache churn;
- degraded kernel scheduling due to concurrent heavy micro-batching from a neighboring workload on the same Dedicated pool (shared host).
- elevated OOM retries causing transient 502/503s which surfaced as client timeouts.

Immediate mitigations applied at 11:30 UTC on 11/3:
- Temporary routing override to isolate MapSync traffic to a cold-start-optimized pool.
- Turned on prefix KV sticky caching for the workload.
- Increased soft capacity by 25% for dedicated nodes serving MapSync.

RCA write-up and logs attached (SLA_VIOLATIONS_LOGS.tar.gz reference). Long-term proposals: move MapSync to a dedicated reserved pool (reduction in noisy neighbor risk), refine scheduling heuristics for sequence-length skew, and implement preemptive detection for sequence-length distribution shifts.

I’ll be on the 16:00 UTC call with MapSync and will bring the logs and a draft remediation timeline.

— Rishi
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
